answer: We define a Sybil-resistant framework where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds utilize zero-knowledge verifiable delay functions and collateralized staking to enforce subgame-perfect slashing matrices. This mechanism instigates a downward utility spiral for adversaries; a fleeting zephyr of identity multiplication triggers a sable liquidation event where expected payoff is purely negative. Protocol convergence occurs as the expense of synthetic cloning exceeds marginal rewards, establishing a strict Nash equilibrium in distributed domains.
